acceptance: Both variable shapes are flagged red first
Reachable codes, and codes from a built binary, stay unflagged
The go/acs corpus test still passes
fix: Extend the scoped bindings with an exit-code value kind: bind a name assigned from a flagged-receiver ExitCode() call or from SubprocessOutput's third result on a go run argv, and compare those names like the call.
summary: evalqualitycheck's go-run-exit-code rule flags only a direct ExitCode() call on a bound go run result. `code := ee.ExitCode(); if code != 3` and `_, _, code, _ := acsassert.SubprocessOutput("go", "run", ...); code != 3` are the same unsatisfiable class and go unflagged. The corpus has no instance today.
title: The go-run exit-code lint follows an exit code copied into a variable or returned by SubprocessOutput
